source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-22

procedures.title: Dwell angle: set (V8 distributor)
steps: Off the car, distributor tester: mount the distributor on the machine, connect the dwell meter to the primary lead and turn the adjusting screw for 30 degrees.
Off the car, test light: clamp the distributor in a vise and connect a test lamp to the primary lead.
Turn the shaft until a cam lobe sits under the center of the breaker lever rubbing block.
Turn the adjusting screw clockwise until the lamp lights, then back it 1/2 turn counterclockwise.

procedures.title: Distributor condenser: test
steps: Use a tester that checks breakdown, insulation leakage, series resistance and capacity, following its maker's instructions.
notes: Breakdown is a direct short through the insulation and stops all condenser action.
Low insulation resistance (leakage) keeps the condenser from holding a charge; some leakage is acceptable.
High series resistance (broken lead strands or a bad connection) burns points and causes failure on first starts and at high speed.
Printed value reads "18-:23 microfarads"; most likely .18-.23 microfarads.

procedures.title: Distributor condenser: replace (V8)
steps: Loosen the condenser lead screw and lift out the lead clip (see figure 6i in the manual).
Remove the screw holding the condenser bracket to the breaker plate and slide the condenser out of the bracket.
Install in reverse order, making sure the new lead sits in the correct position (figure 6i).

procedures.title: Distributor (breaker point type): remove
steps: On radio-equipped Corvettes, remove the ignition shield over the distributor and coil: 1 bolt on top, 2 at the rear facing the firewall.
Release the cap hold-down screws and set the cap aside.
If needed, pull the plug wires from the cap after marking the No. 1 cylinder tower.
Disconnect the distributor primary lead at the coil.
Scribe a mark on the distributor bowl and the engine in line with the rotor segment.
Disconnect the vacuum line and the tachometer drive cable (Corvette).
Remove the hold-down bolt and clamp and lift the distributor out, noting how the vacuum advance unit faces the engine.
Do not turn the engine while the distributor is out, or timing will be lost.

procedures.title: Distributor (breaker point type): disassemble
steps: Before taking it apart, preferably run the distributor on a test machine or synchroscope.
To mount it, clamp the gear in the test drive first, then push the housing down toward the gear to remove end play.
